correctness.rationale: The exposed side normal u of P_n shows that the support segment [v0,v1]+lambda F(K,u) is covered by its two vertex translates only if F(K,u) is a nondegenerate segment and lambda*ell >= 2sin(pi/n). For every other support direction of P_n its exposed face is a vertex, hence already covered. Symmetry rotates the side test to all boundary sides and implies that the origin belongs to one translate iff it belongs to all iff lambda>=gauge_K(-v0). Under both conditions every boundary point of C=P_n+lambda K lies in some convex translate containing origin, so radial filling covers C; the necessities also hold. For K=R_delta P_m, exact normals inclusion requires n|m and delta ≡ pi/n−pi/m (mod 2pi/m); ell=2sin(pi/m), with center gauge giving lambda*=1 (m=n even), sec(pi/n) (m=n odd), or sin(pi/n)/sin(pi/m) (m>n). The m>n side bound dominates gauge by sin(2a)/sin(a)>=sec(a) for a<=pi/6. Independent polygonal computations checked 68 aligned thresholds and support normals; real body theorem follows from the support/radial proof, not floating-point tests.
residual_risks: K must have full n-fold rotation symmetry, nonempty interior, compact convex; not a general asymmetrical-convexifier theorem. Institutional access limitation is bibliographic, not proof failure.
